Start with processed GRAND3 counts and their matching discrete labeling
likelihoods. This example uses a two-hour sci-fate contrast to estimate
bursting kinetics in each condition and ask whether burst frequency, burst
size, or both changed.

| Parameter | Meaning | Units when time is in hours |
|---|---|---|
| `km` | Burst initiation rate | Per hour |
| `B` | Mean transcripts per burst | Molecules per burst |
| `d` | RNA degradation rate | Per hour |
| `lambda = km * B` | Mean synthesis rate | Molecules per hour |

> Supply your own GRAND3 files to run sections 1–3. Section 4 runs on
> constructed draws and shows how to read the comparison output. For a complete
> example with generated inputs, see [acute perturbation](acute_pertubation.html).

```{r packages}
library(buRst)
library(grandR)
```

## 1. Match counts to labeling likelihoods

The full-likelihood fit reads the Binom HDF5 file using the count, gene, and
cell references in the same `.targets` directory.

```text
scifate.targets/
  matrix.mtx.gz
  features.tsv.gz
  barcodes.tsv.gz
  4sU.Binom.discrete.h5
```

Keep the original order and identifiers in the target files. You can filter
genes and cells in the `grandR` object while keeping the original HDF5 and
references. The HDF5 supplies labeling likelihoods directly, so set
`read.posterior = FALSE` when loading the data.

```{r read-input, eval=FALSE}
prefix <- "path/to/scifate"
d <- grandR::ReadGRAND3(prefix, read.posterior = FALSE)
d <- grandR::FilterGenes(d, mincol = 50, minval = 1)
d <- subset(d, no4sU == FALSE)
grandR::Condition(d) <- c("Library", "Sample")

table(grandR::Coldata(d)$Condition)
h5_path <- file.path(paste0(prefix, ".targets"), "4sU.Binom.discrete.h5")
stopifnot(file.exists(h5_path))
```

This template keeps genes detected in at least 50 cells before subsetting to
labeled cells. Use the printed condition labels exactly as they appear in your
data and check that both groups contain cells.

## 2. Fit a two-gene contrast

This example compares A549 cells at 0 h and 2 h. The first condition is a
steady-state reference; the second evolves from that reference after a change
in kinetic parameters.

```{r fit-batch, eval=FALSE}
out <- run_kinetics_batch(
  data = d,
  genes = c("DUSP1", "FKBP5"),
  cond1 = "A549 0h",
  cond2 = "A549 2h",
  t.label = 2,
  t.diff = 2,
  fit1_steady = TRUE,
  fit2_steady = FALSE,
  fit2_ref_cond = "A549 0h",
  h5_path = h5_path,
  ndraw = 20000,
  seed = 123,
  do_compare = TRUE,
  compare_args = list(plot = FALSE, seed = 123),
  parallel = FALSE,
  timeout_sec = 300,
  verbose_every = 1
)
```

> **Transient timing.** Set `t.diff` equal to `t.label`. The model starts with
> the reference RNA population at labeling onset and assumes the kinetic change
> starts then.

Once these fits complete, use the same settings with a larger gene list.
`ndraw` sets the number of local Laplace draws used to summarize uncertainty.

## 3. Check the condition fits

Use the comparison table to find failed fits and comparison errors. The fit
table contains the returned estimates and identification flags. It can be empty
if all fits fail.

```{r inspect-results, eval=FALSE}
out$comparisons
if (nrow(out$fits)) {
  fields <- c("gene", "fit_cond", "km_hat", "B_hat", "d_hat", "conv", "id_flag")
  out$fits[, fields]
}
```

| Output | How to read it |
|---|---|
| `*_hat` | Fitted parameter estimate |
| `*_lo`, `*_med`, `*_hi` | 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles of local Laplace draws |
| `conv` | Optimizer convergence code. Zero indicates convergence. |
| `id_flag` | Identification diagnostic. Inspect `bad_hessian`, `strong_tradeoff`, and missing flags before interpretation. |
| `ok` in comparisons | Whether the required fits and comparison completed |

Check both conditions for each gene. Local Laplace draws approximate the
uncertainty around the fitted optimum. When frequency and size trade off
strongly, the data can support a range of combinations with similar likelihood.

### Retrieve draws for an individual gene

`run_kinetics_batch()` returns compact tables. Use `run_kinetics_fits()` to
retain the fitted objects and their posterior draws:

```{r retain-objects, eval=FALSE}
fits <- run_kinetics_fits(
  data = d, genes = "DUSP1",
  cond1 = "A549 0h", cond2 = "A549 2h",
  t.label = 2, t.diff = 2,
  fit1_steady = TRUE, fit2_steady = FALSE,
  fit2_ref_cond = "A549 0h",
  h5_path = h5_path, ndraw = 20000, seed = 123,
  parallel = FALSE
)
fits$fit_meta

pair <- fits$fit_objects[["DUSP1"]]
if (all(c("A549 0h", "A549 2h") %in% names(pair))) {
  print(fits$fits[, c("fit_cond", "conv", "id_flag")])
}
```

After checking convergence and identification in both conditions, run the
comparison on the retained pair.

```{r compare-one-gene, eval=FALSE}
comparison <- compare_posteriors_gate_star_kmB(
  pair[["A549 0h"]], pair[["A549 2h"]],
  gene = "DUSP1", seed = 123, plot = TRUE
)
comparison$summary
comparison$plot
```

The comparison pairs draws across conditions independently and keeps each
condition's frequency and size draws together. A positive log2 fold change
means the parameter is higher in **condition 2**.

## 4. Read change and mechanism together

The example below constructs correlated draws around a twofold frequency
increase. The points show uncertainty in the two log2 fold changes together.

```{r illustrative-comparison}
set.seed(1)
make_result <- function(km, B, n = 1500) {
  u <- rnorm(n)
  v <- rnorm(n)
  draws <- list(
    km = exp(log(km) + 0.12 * u),
    B = exp(log(B) - 0.08 * u + 0.08 * v)
  )
  structure(data.frame(gene = "illustration"), samples = draws)
}
reference <- make_result(km = 1, B = 2)
perturbed <- make_result(km = 2, B = 2)
comparison <- compare_posteriors_gate_star_kmB(
  reference, perturbed, gene = "Illustrative frequency increase",
  seed = 1, plot = TRUE, max_plot_points = 1000, grid_n = 120
)
fields <- c("call_change", "attrib_ok", "top_mechanism", "mechanism_supported")
knitr::kable(comparison$summary[, fields])
```

```{r plot-comparison, fig.cap="Illustrative joint log2 fold-change draws. The cross marks the posterior medians; colored regions describe the relative contributions of frequency and size."}
comparison$plot + ggplot2::labs(caption = NULL)
```

| Read in this order | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| `call_change` | Whether joint evidence and practical effect size support a change |
| `attrib_ok` | Whether attribution passes the optional interval-width check |
| `mechanism_supported` | Whether the leading mechanism meets the configured support threshold |
| `top_mechanism` | Leading region among the changed draws |

Interpret the leading mechanism when change and attribution are supported.
If `call_change` is true and attribution lacks support, report a change with
unresolved mechanism. Keep failed comparisons separate from completed
comparisons with no supported change.

## 5. Save the results

```{r save-results, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(out, "bursting_results.rds")
```

Keep a record of the fit settings, condition cell counts, and session info so
you can reproduce the comparison.

**Continue with** the [acute-perturbation experiment](acute_pertubation.html)
to see how these checks work with known changes in both parameters.
